instruction: Change the default heading font to Courier New in LibreOffice Writer.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully changed the default font to Times New Roman by navigating to Tools > Options > LibreOffice Writer > Basic Fonts (Western) and modifying the Default font field.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Writer Options dialog, find Basic Fonts settings, select fonts from dropdown, apply and confirm changes.
metadata.task_rationale: Targets the Heading font field instead of Default font, testing whether the model can modify a different font category in the same settings panel.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the heading font to Courier New. Custom metric find_heading_font parses registrymodifications.xcu for the sHeading property under /DefaultFont/Standard path. [Fixed: corrected XPath path from /DefaultFont to /DefaultFont/Standard, and property name from StandardHeading to sHeading]
fix_history: Fix 1: Changed XPath path from '/org.openoffice.Office.Writer/DefaultFont' to '/org.openoffice.Office.Writer/DefaultFont/Standard'
Fix 2: Changed property name from 'StandardHeading' to 'sHeading' to match LibreOffice registrymodifications.xcu schema

llm_judge_reasons: XPath path '/org.openoffice.Office.Writer/DefaultFont/Standard' correctly targets the LibreOffice default font settings group in registrymodifications.xcu.
Property name 'sHeading' correctly identifies the heading font property in the LibreOffice schema.
Namespace handling with 'oor': 'http://openoffice.org/2001/registry' is correct for parsing registrymodifications.xcu.
Parameter handling is correct: metric receives rules dict directly from get_rule and accesses rules['font_name'] without unwrapping.
Full instruction coverage: single requirement (change heading font to Courier New) is fully verified by comparing extracted font value against expected 'Courier New'.
Minor concern: if the heading font was never changed from default, the entry may not exist in registrymodifications.xcu, but this is expected failure behavior for an incomplete task.
